mentions.text: I just passed my 12th and I am extremely confused between JECRC University Jaipur and Lovely Professional University (LPU). I live in MP. At LPU, I am getting a 40% scholarship which brings down the academic fees to around 1.9 Lakhs per year, making it almost identical to JECRC's fees (around 2.3 Lakhs without scholarship). My main concern is placements and crowd. I've heard LPU's intake for B.Tech CSE is absolutely massive (literally thousands of kids in one batch), which makes on-campus placement competition insanely cut-throat. At JECRC, the peer group is average, but the batch size is relatively smaller and more manageable. Mass recruiters like Capgemini, Accenture, and some local Jaipur IT firms visit JECRC regularly, but for high packages, you'll have to try off-campus anyway. Which one should I choose for better placement support and a less crowded environment?
mentions.title: LPU vs JECRC University for BTech CSE: Confused Madhya Pradesh Student
mentions.author: u/willys1999
mentions.summary: An aspiring CSE student compares LPU and JECRC University, expressing concerns over LPU's massive batch size and asking if JECRC offers a less crowded environment with decent placement opportunities.
positives: More manageable batch size compared to LPU's massive intake
Decent local and mass recruitment presence (Capgemini, Accenture)
negatives: High-end product placements mostly require off-campus efforts

mentions.text: If you are planning to join JECRC University Jaipur this year, here is my honest review of the accommodation. The on-campus hostels are actually quite decent, especially the AC suite-style rooms (which have 3 private rooms and a common hall). It's much cleaner and better maintained than what you get at Lovely Professional University or Jaipur National University. However, the hostel fees are rising, and the mess food is just average. Breakfast is the only saving grace (you get sweets 3-4 times a week, but lunch and dinner get repetitive). A lot of students are moving out to PGs and flats near Sitapura, but local PGs are now charging up to ₹11,000 per month, which is crazy expensive for Jaipur. If you are a first-year student, stick to the JECRC hostel for safety and convenience, then shift to a flat in your second year.
mentions.title: Honest JECRC University Hostel Review 2026 - Mess Food, Rules, and Flat Alternatives
mentions.author: See With VISHAL
mentions.summary: An honest breakdown of JECRC University's hostel facilities, highlighting the comfortable AC suites but pointing out rising fees, average mess food, and the high cost of local PGs.
positives: AC suite-style hostel rooms are well-maintained
Good security and convenience for first-year students on campus
negatives: Average mess food (lunch and dinner are repetitive)
Nearby PGs in Sitapura are becoming very expensive (~₹11,000/month)

mentions.text: I'm joining college this session for B.Tech CSE and I'm stuck between Manipal University Jaipur (MUJ) and JECRC University. I've already been working as a freelance web developer and building SaaS projects. Looking at the 4-year fee structures: MUJ is coming up to ~₹29.4 Lakhs total (without scholarship) whereas JECRC is around ~₹16.6 Lakhs total [1.2.4]. I talked to a senior at JECRC who told me that although there is a strict 75% attendance policy on paper, the admin is actually quite chill if you are building real-world projects or freelancing, and some manage with 30% attendance. In MUJ, the shift system (8 AM - 12:30 PM or 1 PM - 4:30 PM) is nice but the strictness and massive fees make me doubt the ROI. Is the MUJ brand really worth spending an extra 13 Lakhs, or should I just save the money, join JECRC, and focus on my own startup/development work?
mentions.title: MUJ CSE vs JECRC CSE - Is the ₹13 Lakh difference worth the ROI?
mentions.author: u/CharacterGoal2384
mentions.summary: A student developer compares the ROI of B.Tech CSE at MUJ (₹29.4L) vs JECRC (₹16.6L), highlighting JECRC's potential flexibility with attendance for active builders.
positives: More affordable fees (~₹16.6 Lakhs total compared to MUJ's ₹29.4L)
Reported flexibility with 75% attendance for students doing freelance/development work
negatives: More traditional full-day structure compared to MUJ's shift system
Lower brand value compared to Manipal

topComplaints.text: Hostel mess food is average and repetitive for lunch and dinner, while hostel fees are rising, pushing students to expensive local PGs.
High-end product placements mostly require off-campus efforts, and the general peer group is perceived as average.

topPraises.text: JECRC offers excellent ROI with significantly lower B.Tech fees (~16.6 Lakhs) compared to Manipal University Jaipur (~29.4 Lakhs).
On-campus AC suite-style hostel rooms are clean, well-maintained, and superior to competitors like LPU and JNU.
The administration is highly flexible with the 75% attendance policy for students actively building real-world projects or freelancing.

strategicRecommendations.title: Formalize and Market the 'Builder Track' Attendance Policy
strategicRecommendations.description: Since student developers highly value JECRC's flexible stance on the 75% attendance rule for active freelancers and startup builders, JECRC should formalize this into a 'Builder Track' policy. This will attract high-caliber, self-driven tech talent who would otherwise choose premium brands like MUJ.
actionableItems: Create an official application process for attendance relaxation based on active freelancing, SaaS development, or startup milestones.
Promote this policy in admissions marketing to position JECRC as the ultimate hub for student entrepreneurs.

strategicRecommendations.title: Revamp Hostel Mess Quality and Stabilize Fees
strategicRecommendations.description: To prevent students from migrating to local PGs in Sitapura, JECRC must address complaints regarding repetitive mess food and rising hostel fees. Improving food variety and offering loyalty discounts for multi-year hostel stays will improve student retention.
actionableItems: Audit the current mess menu and introduce weekly food variations, especially for lunch and dinner.
Introduce a price-lock guarantee or multi-year hostel fee packages to mitigate the perception of rising costs.

strategicRecommendations.title: Leverage 'Manageable Batch Size' in Competitive Marketing
strategicRecommendations.description: Prospective students are actively worried about the massive, hyper-competitive batch sizes at LPU. JECRC should design marketing campaigns that highlight its manageable batch sizes, which lead to personalized placement support and less cut-throat on-campus competition.
actionableItems: Publish comparative marketing materials highlighting student-to-placement-coordinator ratios.
Emphasize the presence of consistent mass recruiters (Capgemini, Accenture) combined with a less crowded campus environment.
